text:
Skill doc shrinks to the invariant core (~40 lines). Only what must be true in every phase: scale contract, claim/dismiss, the request loop, "the seat is the complete capability surface, never bun/python," refusal semantics, and "before any work: seat oracle start <task description>." Everything else moves behind the oracle.

oracle start classifies the task and returns a plan:

Bash
tools/seat oracle start "retopologize this Tripo soup into a skinnable prop"
# → { plan: ["setup","retopo","naming","uv-skin","finish"],
#     phase: "setup",
#     doc: <the setup section — claim, look, ghost-freeze, target metrics>,
#     checklist: [...], exitCriteria: [...] }
Different tasks get different plans: a blockout task never loads the retopo corridor doc; a rig task loads rig gates and pointers back to topology repair only if connected_body fails. Context cost tracks the actual task.

Each phase returns three things: the doc slice, the checklist, and machine-checkable exit criteria. That last one is the load-bearing part:

Bash
tools/seat oracle status
# → { phase: "topology",
#     checks: [
#       {id:"junctions-resolved", verified:"host", pass:false,
#        detail:"3 shell pairs with bit-identical contact planes and surviving mating faces"},
#       {id:"unreachable-pct", verified:"host", pass:false, detail:"31% > 5% budget"},
#       {id:"seams-welded", verified:"agent-attest", pass:null}
#     ],
#     next:"naming", blocked:true }
tools/seat oracle advance
# refuses with the exact failing checks — same voice as save refusing unnamed faces
Host-verified checks come from the audit machinery you're already building (select-audit, shell counts, junction detection, rig-status rows, semantic-status). Agent-attested checks exist only where no measurement exists yet — and each one is a filed feature request for a future audit, exactly like the bun-escape signal.

Design rules that make it work
Never hide an invariant a phase needs early. The classic failure of phased docs: "name at the operation that creates it" is a modeling-phase behavior even though naming has its own phase. Solve this by making each phase doc carry its forward obligations explicitly — the modeling phase says "name every extrude now; the naming phase only audits and refines." The phase system must never teach an agent to defer debt to the phase where the debt is checked.

advance is a gate, not a page-turn. Refusal carries the failing checks with counts and selectable evidence (select-audit-style). Passing hands back the next phase's doc in the same reply — the agent never has to remember to fetch it.

Allow lookups without phase changes. Mid-phase, an agent hits a UV question during topology work. seat oracle ask "uv stitch requirements" returns the relevant slice without touching the plan. Routing ≠ state.

Put phase in the percept. One field — "oracle":{"phase":"topology","blocked":2} — so every single reply reminds the agent where it is and how much debt stands between it and the next phase. This is your unnamed counter pattern: ambient, unavoidable, per-reply.

Interruption-proof it. Phase state must survive reconnects and be reconstructible: a cold agent runs oracle status and gets the plan, current phase, and live check results — the same "a cold agent must be able to continue from look alone" discipline, extended to workflow position. Since most checks are host-computed from the actual model, phase state is mostly derived, not stored, which is why this survives cold restarts for free.

What this buys you beyond context savings
The subtle win: the oracle becomes the place process improvements land. Today, fixing agent behavior means editing a monolithic doc and hoping the next agent reads the right paragraph. With phased gates, fixing behavior means adding a check to a phase — and every agent hits it, because advance refuses. Your measured disasters map directly: the 43%-unreachable epidemic becomes unreachable-pct blocking the topology→naming transition; the 175-regions-over-300-faces noise becomes a naming-density check; fake merges become a junction check that part-merge cannot satisfy because it's measured on geometry, not rows.

One warning: keep oracle start cheap and the setup phase tiny, or agents under time pressure will skip the oracle entirely and work from stale memory of the old monolith. The first phase should be faster than not using the oracle — claim + look + scale declaration, three commands — so the path of least resistance runs through the gate machine from the first minute. Same principle as everything else here: the sanctioned path must be shorter than the workaround.
resolution: Replaced the two monolithic skill documents with a phase-gate oracle. agent-seat's 1173 lines and agent-skin's 180 became one corpus of 12 markdown phase slices under .agents/skills/agent-seat/corpus/, routed by cart/editor/agent/seatOracle.ts and reached as tools/seat oracle start|status|advance|attest|ask|stop|plans. A task is classified into one of five plans, so a retopo job loads setup/retopo/naming/uv-skin/finish and never pays for the blockout corridor. advance is a gate, not a page-turn: exit criteria are host-measured from the live model, pass:null blocks because unknown is not clean, and a host-measured check cannot be attested past — attestation exists only where no audit exists yet and each one is a filed feature request. The measured disasters became checks: 43%-unreachable now blocks topology to naming, and 175-regions-over-300 blocks naming on a density ceiling with a sample floor. Each phase carries explicit forward obligations so the system never teaches agents to defer debt to the phase that checks it, percept.oracle rides every reply as an ambient counter, and the plan cursor rides the Follow hot-state twig so a hot reload no longer drops an agent mid-plan. SKILL.md is now 70 lines of invariant core. Verified live end to end plus 18 new router tests.
